rationale: Map refresh and protection analysis after the fifth obligation was answered in scope. Two premises are cleared because they are answered: the configuration fact's question about whether the client-visible configuration future reports the index at which the configuration was established (answered by the served check), and the follower-match fact's question about whether a match recorded for a peer that is concurrently removed from the latest configuration can still contribute to a commit decision before the commitment table is rebuilt. The second answer is a bounded negative reached by reading rather than by execution: the leader appends the configuration entry, then replaces the copy of the latest configuration, then rebuilds the commitment table, all as adjacent statements on the main goroutine, and configuration changes are admitted only when the previous one is committed so that at most one is uncommitted at a time; a match that lands inside that window is counted against the voter set the table still holds, and because the old and the new quorum of a one-at-a-time change always intersect, any index committed there is also held by a quorum of the resulting configuration. That reasoning is recorded as a protection on the commitment behavior, with its sources, instead of being left as an open question. The surface that recorded the configuration index is kept but moved from deferred to mapped against the client contract behavior that reports it, and the overview, facts and behaviors otherwise keep their assertions, identities, contexts and edges.

feedback.answered: Two frontier questions are answered. First, the client-visible configuration index: the accessor builds its future from the copy of the latest configuration and never sets that value's index, while the same field is published as latest_configuration_index in Stats, and a served check on a bootstrapped single-voter node observed a reported index of zero against a configuration established at index 1, so the fact's question about whether the accessor reports where the configuration was established is settled. Second, the follower-match timing question is answered by reading rather than execution: the configuration entry is appended, the latest configuration is replaced and the commitment table rebuilt as adjacent statements on the main goroutine, and because changes are admitted only when the previous one is committed, a match counted inside that window uses the old voter set whose quorum intersects the new one, so no index can be committed there that the resulting configuration would not also hold.
